chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: 'Ibbad ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:'
I said: 'May I be your sacrifice, [what is the meaning of] 'Yet, he has not entered into Aqaba'.'
He said: 'Whoever Allah honors with our Wilayah (guardianship) has passed the Aqaba. We are that Aqaba. Whoever enters it will be saved.'
He said: 'Then he fell silent, and then said: 'Shall I inform you of a letter/word that is better than the world and all that is in it?''
I said: 'Yes, may I be your sacrifice.'
He said: 'His saying, Exalted is He: 'The freeing of a neck/slave.''
All people are slaves of the Fire, except you and your companions. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has freed your necks from the Fire through our Wilayah, the People of the House.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْت: The People of the House, referring to the Prophet's family and Imams
key_terms.الْعَقَبَة: The obstacle or step, interpreted here as the Wilayah of the Imams
key_terms.عِبَادُ النَّار: Slaves of the Fire, referring to those destined for Hell
key_terms.فُكُّ رَقَبَة: Freeing of a neck/slave, interpreted as liberation from Hellfire
key_terms.وِلَايَة: Divine guardianship or authority, specifically of the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Aqaba' in Surah Al-Balad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Fadail al-Shia, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the 'Aqaba' (steep path) in Surah Al-Balad as the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt, asserting that acceptance of this divine guardianship constitutes the primary act of salvation. He further interprets 'freeing a neck' (Fakk Rakaba) not merely as manumission, but as the spiritual liberation of the faithful from the fire of Hell through their connection to the Imams. This interpretation underscores the Shia theological view that Wilayah is the essential criterion for deliverance from eternal punishment.
